Di means “of / from”.

recall.q: How do you say “with” in Italian?

Per means “for”.

stage.sub: Formal relative 'il quale': il quale, la quale.

recall.q: Which form fits a feminine singular noun?

recall.q: “The book that I read”
“The girl who speaks”

stage.name: AVOID_NOUN_RESTATEMENT

stage.title: Non-restrictive relative clauses (comma-separated, extra information)

stage.sub: Distinguishing restrictive from non-restrictive relative clauses.

DIFFERENT_SUBJECT_CONDITION.t: Condition: subject of main clause differs from subject of dependent clause

stage.name: DIFFERENT_SUBJECT_CONDITION
stage.title: Condition: subject of main clause differs from subject of dependent clause
stage.sub: Condition: subject of main clause differs from subject of dependent clause.

recall.q: In “Spero che tu venga”, are the subjects different?

script.text:
The subjunctive is used when the subject of the main clause is different from the subject of the che-clause: Penso che Marco sia a casa (I think, and Marco is at home).
Two different subjects: io and Marco.

script.q: In “Spero che tu venga”, are the subjects different?
script.hint: Not quite. Look back at the card above.

recall.q: “I think he is right”

script.text:
Verbs of opinion trigger the subjunctive: Penso che sia vero means “I think it is true”.
Credo che, penso che and mi sembra che are the usual openers.

script.q: “I think he is right”
script.hint: Not quite. Look back at the card above.

recall.q: “I doubt that he is here”

script.text:

recall.q: “I hope you are well”

CORE_RULE.t: Core rule: subjunctive after che-clause when main clause expresses opinion/doubt/emotion/desire/necessity and subjects differ

stage.name: CORE_RULE
stage.title: Core rule
stage.sub: Core rule: subjunctive after che-clause when main clause expresses opinion/doubt/emotion/desire/necessity and subjects differ.

recall.q: Which of these needs the subjunctive?

script.text:
The core rule: use the subjunctive after che when the main clause expresses an opinion, a doubt, an emotion, a desire or a necessity, and the two subjects are different.
Penso che sia vero (opinion). Dubito che venga (doubt). Ho paura che piova (emotion). Spero che tu stia bene (desire). È importante che tu studi (necessity).

stage.sub: Verbs of certainty/fact (so che, e vero che) take the indicative, not subjunctive.

stage.sub: Recognising same-subject case: no subjunctive needed.

recall.q: In “Spero di venire”, is the subjunctive needed?

script.text:
If the subject of both clauses is the same, you do not use the subjunctive. In Credo di avere ragione, the one who believes and the one who is right are both “I”.
The subjunctive needs two different subjects.

script.q: In “Spero di venire”, is the subjunctive needed?

recall.q: “I think I am right”

script.text:

stage.sub: Concept of transitive verbs (needed to form a passive).

recall.q: Which verb can be made passive?

script.text:
Only transitive verbs, which take a direct object, can be made passive: Marco legge il libro becomes Il libro è letto da Marco.
Verbs like andare or dormire have no object, so they have no passive.

stage.name: SIMPLE_TENSES

stage.title: Concept of simple vs compound tenses
stage.sub: Concept of simple vs compound tenses.

recall.q: Which is a simple tense?

The sequence of tenses: main clause in the present + simultaneous action = present subjunctive (Penso che mangi); present + earlier action = past subjunctive (Penso che abbia mangiato).
Main clause in the past or conditional + simultaneous = imperfect subjunctive (Pensavo che mangiasse); past + earlier = pluperfect subjunctive (Pensavo che avesse mangiato).

script.q: Main clause “Pensavo che...”, simultaneous action. Which verb?
script.hint: Not quite. Look back at the card above.

script.q: Main clause “Penso che...”, earlier action. Which verb?

recall.q: “If you study, you pass”

script.text:
The present indicative states facts and habits: Studio ogni giorno means “I study every day”.
It is the tense of the se-clause in a real condition: Se studi, passi l’esame.

script.q: “If you study, you pass”
script.hint: Not quite. Look back at the card above.

recall.q: “I will study”

script.text:
The future states what will happen: Studierò domani means “I will study tomorrow”.
It can appear in the result of a real condition: Se studi, passerai l’esame.

script.q: “I will study”
script.hint: Not quite. Look back at the card above.

recall.q: “If I studied”

script.text:
The imperfect subjunctive is used in the se-clause of a possible or unlikely condition: Se studiassi, passerei l’esame means “If I studied, I would pass the exam”.
Its forms: studiassi, studiassi, studiasse, studiassimo, studiaste, studiassero.

script.q: “If I studied”
script.hint: Not quite. Look back at the card above.

recall.q: “I would pass”

script.text:
The present conditional says what would happen: passerei means “I would pass”.
It is the verb of the result clause in a possible condition: Se studiassi, passerei l’esame.

script.q: “I would pass”
script.hint: Not quite. Look back at the card above.

recall.q: “If I had studied”

script.text:
The pluperfect subjunctive is the imperfect subjunctive of avere or essere plus the participle: avessi studiato, fossi andato.
It is used in the se-clause of an impossible condition (one that did not happen).

script.q: “If I had studied”
script.hint: Not quite. Look back at the card above.

recall.q: “I would have passed”

script.text:
The past conditional says what would have happened: avrei passato means “I would have passed”.
It is the verb of the result clause in an impossible condition.

script.q: “I would have passed”
script.hint: Not quite. Look back at the card above.

recall.q: Which is more suited to a formal essay?

script.text:
Register is how formal your language is. Written and formal Italian uses full forms and connectors; spoken Italian is looser and uses contractions and fillers.
A formal essay avoids spoken shortcuts that you would use with a friend.

recall.q: Which is the more formal verb for “to understand”?

script.text:
Some words are more formal than their everyday partners: comprendere (to understand, formal) vs capire (everyday); iniziare vs cominciare; ottenere vs prendere.
In a formal text, comprendere is the better choice, and with friends you would say capire.

recall.q: Which connector takes the subjunctive?

script.text:
The present subjunctive is used after expressions of opinion, doubt, emotion, desire and necessity, and after connectors like sebbene and nonostante: Penso che sia vero; Sebbene piova, esco.
Its forms: che io parli, che lui prenda, che lui dorma.

recall.q: How do you say “however” in Italian?

script.text:
Tuttavia means “however”.
Tuttavia is a formal connector: Il progetto è utile; tuttavia, è costoso means “The project is useful; however, it is expensive”.

recall.q: How do you say “therefore” in Italian?
How do you say “so / therefore” in Italian?

script.text:
Quindi means “therefore”.
Dunque means “so / therefore”.
Penso, dunque sono is “I think, therefore I am”. Quindi is the everyday “therefore”.

recall.q: What word means “despite”?

script.text:
Nonostante means “despite” or “although”. With a clause it takes the subjunctive: Nonostante piova, esco means “Although it is raining, I am going out”.
With a noun, no subjunctive is needed: nonostante la pioggia.

recall.q: Which is better in a formal essay?

script.text:
In formal writing, avoid spoken shortcuts such as “cioè”, “tipo”, “boh” and clipped forms. Choose full, neutral words and connectors instead.
Write Tuttavia rather than Però when you want a more formal tone.

recall.q: Which sentence is a thesis?
recall.a: Il lavoro da remoto migliora la qualità della vita

script.text:
A thesis statement is the main claim of your paragraph, stated clearly at the start: Il lavoro da remoto migliora la qualità della vita means “Working from home improves quality of life”.
Everything after it supports or limits that claim.
